title: Hash Keys and Symbols
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of hash keys and symbols in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply hash keys and symbols in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to key equality and consistency and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Hash Keys and Symbols through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding hash keys and symbols helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Hash Keys and Symbols helps you reason about symbol-keyed hashes. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Symbol-keyed hashes. Then connect it to String keys. The remaining syllabus points—Key equality and consistency—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Run the example as written, compare it with the expected result, and explain why each line supports hash keys and symbols. Next change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a second example for hash keys and symbols using a different input. Add one edge case from the syllabus list (Key equality and consistency), state the expected behavior, and write a small test or manual check that would catch a regression.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain hash keys and symbols, identify its place in hashes, sets, and ranges, run a focused example, and verify an important boundary. Revisit the linked exercise if this is a core topic; advanced runtime or framework examples remain draft until reviewed in a suitable environment.
